response_json.request: Add rectangular openining to the lower back of the coffee machine, which might serve as draft location for plug and main ON/OFF switch. Opening should be 20cm x 10cm and 3cm deep rectangle with roundend corners (radius 1cm). Position should be more or less equally distanced from bottom and sides of the device.

actions.operation: Create a rounded-rectangular opening extending 3 cm into the lower back of the coffee machine.
actions.target: Lower region of the rear exterior cover of the main housing. The semantic back direction is -Y with confidence 0.99, so the opening is created from the -Y-facing rear surface and cut inward toward +Y.
actions.relational_constraint: Orient the 20 cm dimension horizontally along X and the 10 cm dimension vertically along Z. Center the opening between the left and right housing boundaries so both lateral margins are equal. Place it in the lower rear region and use an approximately equal or visually balanced clearance from the bottom boundary and lateral sides, while maintaining material around the lower rounded shell transition and feet.
actions.unresolved_reference: The exact rear-cover width, bottom datum elevation, wall thickness, internal-component clearance, and numerical edge margin are not supplied. The phrase 'more or less equally distanced' is approximate. Use a centered horizontal constraint and a parameterized vertical offset; confirm that a 200 mm by 100 mm profile fits within the rear cover and that a 30 mm blind cut does not unintentionally intersect the base frame, feet, rear ventilation assembly, rails, or internal components.
steps: Modify section S01, Main housing and base frame. Do not create a separate model section and do not remove S02, because the requested feature is an opening in the structural outer enclosure rather than a modification to the ventilation-hole or guard-rail arrays.

Use the semantic orientation to resolve the requested back side: back maps to CAD axis -Y at 0.99 confidence. Select the Rear cover exterior face_code 0008, corresponding to Brep_id FACE 90, as the primary placement face.

Inspect the -Y view and the rear-cover body to identify the usable lower planar or near-planar field. Preserve clearance from the rounded perimeter, bottom shell transition, corner feet, cover seams, and any mounting features.

If face 0008 is sufficiently planar, create the sketch directly on it. If it is curved or blended, create an XZ datum plane tangent to, or offset immediately outside, the central rear exterior field. Set the sketch normal so the cutting direction points inward along +Y.
Project or reference the rear cover's left and right usable boundaries and its lower usable boundary into the sketch. Add a vertical construction centerline on the machine X center plane.

Sketch a closed rounded rectangle with an overall width of 200 mm along X, an overall height of 100 mm along Z, and four tangent corner arcs of 10 mm radius. Use either a centered rounded-rectangle tool or four straight segments joined by tangent 10 mm sketch fillets.
Constrain the profile symmetrically about the machine X center plane so the left and right margins are equal. Keep the profile horizontal and vertical relative to the global X and Z axes.

Locate the profile in the lower rear region. Parameterize the bottom clearance rather than fixing an unsupported value. Where the rear-cover dimensions permit, set the bottom clearance approximately equal to the lateral clearance calculated from the usable rear width; otherwise use the nearest visually balanced lower position that preserves adequate structural edge distance.

Validate that the 200 mm width and 100 mm height remain entirely inside the usable rear-cover field and do not cross the side perimeter blends, lower bridge, cover attachment features, or feet. If the specified size cannot fit, report the dimensional conflict rather than silently reducing the opening.

Create a blind pocket or subtractive extrusion from the rounded-rectangle profile, directed inward toward +Y, with a depth of 30 mm. Interpret the stated 3 cm depth as a blind cut, not a through-all cut.

Limit the Boolean subtraction to the intended S01 rear-cover or housing body. Do not cut S02 ventilation slats, perforated panel, guard rails, cups, brew group, steam wand, console, or operating lever unless the design is explicitly revised to require penetration through those components.

Where a curved rear surface causes nonuniform local engagement, start the cutter from the exterior tangent datum and extend it far enough to produce a clean 30 mm axial depth measured along +Y. Confirm that the resulting entrance boundary remains the specified 200 mm by 100 mm rounded rectangle when viewed normal to the rear.

Inspect the resulting pocket walls and floor for accidental breakthroughs or zero-thickness regions. In particular, check possible interaction with the Rear housing interface face_code 0007, Brep_id FACE 87, and stop or revise the depth if the 30 mm cut would compromise an unintended internal structural member.

Do not add an unspecified edge fillet or chamfer to the opening. The required 10 mm radius applies to the four plan-view corners of the rounded rectangle, not to the front rim edges through the cut depth.

Recompute the model and verify from the -Y view that the opening is horizontally centered and visibly located in the lower rear region. Verify from the +X and -X views that the cut extends 30 mm inward along +Y and retains adequate material above the base and around the rear perimeter.

Perform final interference and manufacturability checks for the intended plug and main ON/OFF switch location, including internal clearance, minimum wall thickness, electrical mounting depth, cable routing space, and separation from ventilation and load-bearing features.

intention: Provide a possible location for a plug and the main ON/OFF switch.
